subject: Reasoning
description: Statement-pairs requiring identification of cause vs effect vs independence

questions.stem:
Statements: I. Heavy monsoon rainfall flooded several villages in the district last week.
II. Many residents have moved to relief camps set up by the local administration.
Which is correct?

options.option_text: Both statements are unrelated independent events
Statement I is the cause and II is the effect
Statement II is the cause and I is the effect
Both are effects of an unstated common cause

questions.explanation: Floods → forced displacement → relief camps. Clear causal direction: I causes II. Distractor 1 ignores the obvious link. Distractor 3 reverses the direction. Distractor 4 assumes a hidden cause when the visible cause-effect pairing is sufficient.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: I. The state government has announced a hike in petrol tax effective next month.
II. Auto-rickshaw unions have called a one-day strike across major cities.
Which is correct?

options.option_text: Both statements are unrelated and coincidental
Statement I is the cause and II is the effect
Statement II is the cause and I is the effect
Both are effects of a separate prior decision

questions.explanation: Fuel-tax hike directly raises costs for auto-rickshaw operators → strike to demand a reversal or fare hike. Cause-effect direction is I → II. Distractor 1 ignores the link. Distractor 3 reverses the order — strikes don't trigger tax announcements after the fact. Distractor 4 assumes a hidden cause unnecessarily.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: I. The school management has reduced the annual fees by ten percent.
II. The school's new sports complex has been inaugurated this week.
Which is correct?

options.option_text: Statement I is the cause and II is the effect
Both are unrelated independent events
Statement II is the cause and I is the effect
Both effects share a common hidden cause

questions.explanation: Fee reduction and a new sports complex are not causally linked — fee cuts would, if anything, REDUCE the budget for new infrastructure (so I cannot cause II). The two announcements are administratively independent. Distractor 1 — opposite of expected; building infrastructure usually requires raising, not lowering, fees. Distractor 3 — the sports complex would not cause a fee cut; if anything the opposite. Distractor 4 — possible only with extra context not provided.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: I. The water levels in the reservoir have dropped sharply this summer.
II. The municipal corporation has announced rationing of household water supply.
Which is correct?

options.option_text: Both are independent events without any link
Statement I is the cause and II is the effect
Statement II is the cause and I is the effect
Both are caused by an unstated administrative reform

questions.explanation: Reservoir level falls → less water in supply → administration rations. I directly causes II. Distractor 1 ignores the obvious link. Distractor 3 reverses cause and effect — rationing doesn't lower a reservoir, drought does. Distractor 4 invokes unnecessary hidden cause.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: I. There has been a 30% rise in the cost of imported electronics this quarter.
II. The Reserve Bank has just allowed the rupee to depreciate against the dollar.
Which is correct?

options.option_text: Both statements are unrelated independent events
Statement II is the cause and I is the effect
Statement I is the cause and II is the effect
Both are caused by foreign-policy decisions abroad

questions.explanation: Rupee depreciation → imports cost more in rupee terms → consumer electronics prices rise. II → I. Distractor 1 misses the macro-link. Distractor 3 reverses direction — a price rise in imported goods doesn't trigger central-bank devaluation. Distractor 4 oversimplifies.

questions.stem:
Statements: I. Farmers in the district have switched from paddy to less water-intensive millets.
II. The groundwater table in the district has begun to recover this year.
Which is correct?

options.option_text: Both are unrelated independent observations
Statement I is the cause and II is the effect
Statement II is the cause and I is the effect
Both are due to higher than normal rainfall this year

questions.explanation: Switching from paddy (very water-intensive) to millet (drought-hardy) reduces groundwater pumping → table recovers. Cause is I, effect is II. Distractor 3 reverses — a recovering groundwater table would NOT push farmers to drier crops; if anything it'd reverse. Distractor 4 is plausible but the question gives no rainfall data; the most direct explanation is the crop switch.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: I. The traffic police have started using AI-powered cameras to issue speeding tickets.
II. Average vehicle speed on the city ring road has dropped this month.
Which is correct?

options.option_text: Both events are independent of each other
Statement I is the cause and II is the effect
Statement II is the cause and I is the effect
Both are caused by a separate awareness campaign

questions.explanation: Stricter automated enforcement → drivers slow down to avoid tickets → average speed drops. I → II. Distractor 3 reverses — drop in speed wouldn't cause new camera installation, although they MIGHT correlate if both arose from a recent crash, that's not in the statements. Distractor 4 invokes an external cause not given.
